scope_notes: agent-tool profile: a token-compression engine, CLI, proxy and MCP server that agents call; uses_crypto true (SigV4, OIDC JWT, TLS, AES) and parses_untrusted true (compresses tool/web payloads); has_ui false (CLI/engine, no GUI); heavy_compute false.

PUR-1.note: README states the problem, users, one-command install, measured results and explicit non-goals ('never touches your prompt'); INSTALL.md is a 30+ agent matrix. No machine-readable capability statement (SKILL.md is prose).

PUR-2.note: A 3-arm eval harness and snapshot are committed with stated limits (n=10, single run); HONEST-NUMBERS reports method and net-negative cases. The flagship 33.2% session number is an older-engine run with no committed raw result (benchmarks/results/.gitkeep).

PUR-3.note: Six 'rocks' and several packages, each with a documented purpose and ownership routing in CLAUDE.md; browse/ is a declared consumer copy and skills are CI-mirrored into plugins/. No necessity gate on new components.

COR-1.note: 697 test files, test/source 1.137; CI runs go test (-race on store/middleware), npm test and pytest across an OS matrix with conformance lanes, gated before merge. No coverage threshold (so not horizon).

COR-2.note: 112 golden/fixture files, TOON encode/decode round-trip, byte-safe invariants and SDK/middleware parity fixtures exercised against a real proxy in CI. Not full differential-vs-reference-tool.

COR-3.note: Go fuzz targets with committed corpora cover the parsers and cache/translate invariants (TOON round-trip, axtree, cache-prefix, responses/messages, scan-string) plus property-style invariants; no mutation testing and no per-release fuzz thresholds.

COR-4.note: caveman-compress is benchmarked on its own memory-file fixtures, release-smoke exercises the shipped binary, and Blocks scans the repo's own agent history; realistic inputs including the tool's own artifacts.

COR-5.note: Core transforms are deterministic: CCR handles are content-addressed (sha256) and idempotent, TOON round-trips, and SBOMs are generated reproducibly. LLM routing is nondeterministic but isolated behind the proxy.

REL-1.note: The CCR recovery store is SQLite in WAL mode with busy_timeout, atomic rename, PERSIST_WAL and reopen-race handling, and fails closed with ErrStorageChanged when the DB identity changes; content-addressed handles make re-processing idempotent. Requests are the unit of work, so there is no long-task resume concept.

REL-2.note: MCP inbound and result payloads are capped at 16 MiB, the CCR store enforces a payload budget (ErrBudgetExceeded) and compressors stream/bound output; large inputs degrade to byte-safe passthrough rather than failing.

REL-3.note: On any parse problem the engine passes bytes through untouched (documented contract); elision markers state the facts computed from dropped units rather than hiding them; MCP tool errors fail closed.

REL-4.note: 80 signal/shutdown references across 67 files, including proxy graceful shutdown and portable child-process management.

PERF-1.note: Benchmarks measure token reduction and a browse page benchmark, but there are no p50/p99 latency budgets for the proxy/engine, which sit on every request.

PERF-2.note: Attention economy is the product: token reduction is measured per file type and per session with tiktoken o200k, outputs are summary-first with CCR retrieval handles for detail, and caveman stats reports token cost. Not fully 'every output states its cost' at the API layer.

SEC-1.note: SECURITY.md gives supported-version lines, a response policy (3-day ack, 30-day critical-fix target), private vulnerability reporting and a per-surface data-flow/threat summary. Disclosure timelines are stated as targets, not measured, so not horizon.

SEC-2.note: Lockfiles for pnpm/go/npm/python, dependabot, and CI known-vulnerability scanning via govulncheck (reachability-based) + pip-audit + npm audit + CodeQL, with certified vs experimental gating.

SEC-3.note: npm/PyPI trusted-publishing provenance, keyless cosign signatures for the GHCR image, docker buildx --provenance --sbom, optional platform code-signing, all from SHA-pinned CI. Short of a documented SLSA L3 / reproducible-build claim.

SEC-4.note: CycloneDX SBOMs generated per release for npm and PyPI and a docker --sbom, with NOTICE and LICENSING.md present. No VEX statements for known CVEs.

SEC-5.note: Actions pinned by full SHA, least-privilege permissions, OpenSSF Scorecard with publish_results and CodeQL; the scorecard workflow is kept minimal (no top-level env, read-all) per its own guidance.

SEC-6.note: RED LINE: not triggered. The 39 secret-like strings are all in tests (well-known AWS doc example keys such as AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE) or are secret-prefix allowlists in detection/redaction code (redact.go, residual.go, repointel/index.go) - independently confirmed, none real. A dedicated redact module scrubs payloads. Below meets: no secret scanner gate in repo CI.

SEC-7.note: RED LINE: not triggered. Go/TS code is free of TLS-off and unsafe-deserialization outside tests; OIDC verification rejects alg=none and HMAC with a public key set, and the wallet npx runs with --ignore-scripts and isolated config. No injection-prone operation on an untrusted path.

SEC-8.note: Untrusted payloads are parsed in memory-safe Go with byte-safe passthrough on any parse error, 16 MiB size caps and committed fuzz corpora on the parsers. Not clearly continuous fuzzing or least-privilege-isolated, so not horizon.

SEC-9.note: Standard-library crypto only (sha256/hmac/tls/ecdsa/rsa/aes/subtle), correct current algorithms (RS256/ES256, AWS4-HMAC-SHA256, constant-time compares) and no deprecated algorithms, but no documented algorithm inventory, replaceable abstraction layer or post-quantum plan.

AGT-1.note: caveman compresses tool output and web pages and never executes them, and the voice 'never touches your prompt', so instruction-following risk is low; but browse/compress and Auto ingest untrusted content with no untrusted-channel marking or injection regression test.

AGT-2.note: Blocks 'never denies or rewrites a command' and routing only changes model/effort, so agency is modest; but there are no machine-checkable per-tool effect declarations and wallet/topup is the only action with an explicit approval.

AGT-3.note: 'caveman learn implement' applies fixes only on an explicit yes, telemetry/routing have off switches, and caveman stats makes token/warm-cache activity visible; readable controls and approvals, though no central action log.

AGT-4.note: A 3-arm eval harness plus a fidelity eval (fixed cases, kept-numbers/negation/safety checks for every arm) exist with a committed snapshot and Cloud autopilot evals; no committed fidelity snapshot, so quality-equivalence is not yet published.

AGT-5.note: SECURITY.md documents, field by field, exactly what Auto/routing/managed modes send to Caveman Cloud and which providers requests go to; providers are catalogued. No model card (caveman ships no model) and no AI-BOM.

AGT-6.note: Token accounting is the product: caveman stats reports usage, Auto trades effort for cost per ask and the engine bounds payloads; per-task hard budgets are not enforced by caveman itself (it is a proxy/engine).

INT-1.note: An MCP stdio server, a CLI with JSON output, TypeScript and Python SDKs and framework middleware adapters; multiple open interfaces, though no stated version/compatibility policy for the CLI surface.

INT-2.note: MCP tools carry name/description/InputSchema and the CLI has --json output and 28 SKILL.md packs; stable field names via a declarative contract. No describe --json manifest of the whole CLI and no contract-drift gate.

INT-3.note: The MCP surface is five composable engine tools (compress/retrieve/stats/toon_encode/toon_decode) with 16 MiB caps, and Blocks ships eight primitives; small and parameterised rather than one tool per case.

INT-4.note: MCP uses stable cave_* snake-case error codes, fails closed on panics/oversize, and the SDK surfaces typed errors; retryable classification exists. Not a single documented cross-surface error schema.

INT-5.note: CCR recovery handles are content-addressed sha256 (idempotent, stored once), scope state carries epochs/receipts/grants, and TOON is deterministic, so results are stable and retriable by handle.

INT-6.note: One-command npx quickstart, a 30+ agent install matrix and a caveman doctor make the CLI ergonomic; there is no GUI to audit for WCAG and no localisation need stated.

INT-7.note: Open, documented outputs: TOON, JSON, CycloneDX SBOM, local CCR store and markdown; data is portable and the originals always stay on disk.

EPI-1.note: Compression outputs are recoverable to the exact original bytes via content-addressed CCR handles, and Cloud 'Proof' marks each number measured/inferred/verified with receipts; every lossy transform records its original.

EPI-2.note: HONEST-NUMBERS labels each number measured/inferred/'not measured yet'; elision markers state computed facts rather than guesses; Cloud distinguishes measured from inferred savings.

EPI-3.note: Elision markers enumerate even absent fields as absent-count buckets so counts reconcile, any parse failure is passed through rather than silently dropped, and caveman stats reports savings as unknown rather than zero when there is no comparison.

EPI-4.note: HONEST-NUMBERS separates when-it-wins from net-negative cases and per-file vs whole-session scope, and the evals README states what each snapshot does and does not cover; coverage is narrated rather than machine-reconciled.

EPI-5.note: RED LINE: not triggered. Headline numbers link to method docs/benchmarks, limitations sit beside the claims (HTML row marked worse, stale snapshots flagged, net-negative issues cited), and CLAUDE.md forbids publishing an unreviewed percentage. Not auto-generated/CI-gated, so not horizon.

MNT-1.note: CLAUDE.md documents the layout and ownership routing and the engine uses leaf packages (e.g. safety has no engine dependency) to avoid import cycles; boundaries are documented but not CI-enforced.

MNT-2.note: Largest source 2840 lines and only 0.71% duplicated bytes by the probe, but skills are mirrored into plugins/caveman/skills, browse/ is a consumer copy and the Apache text is repeated across many directories (~86 duplicate files), so intentional mirrors can drift.

MNT-3.note: TypeScript type-checking (tsc --noEmit) and go vet run, with .editorconfig for format, but there is no golangci-lint/staticcheck, no gofmt gate, no ESLint and no Python linter or type checker across 93k lines of Go, 41k TS and 22k Py.

MNT-4.note: An extensive CLAUDE.md (plus per-directory CLAUDE/AGENTS), AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, CONTRIBUTING and a docs site document the repo for maintainers and agents; no architecture decision records.

MNT-5.note: Only two TODO markers in the probe and CLAUDE.md records structural debt (the browse consumer copy, mirrored skills) in prose, but there is no debt ledger with repayment triggers.

EVO-1.note: Ten independently-versioned packages with a stated SemVer policy for the SDK/middleware 1.x line, but no top-level CHANGELOG or migration guides and version meaning across the monorepo is not uniform.

EVO-2.note: Releases are automated with SBOMs, signing, digest-checked artifacts and a release-smoke qualification; release notes are generated per tag and a provider-catalog changelog exists, though there is no single product changelog.

EVO-3.note: CI and release matrices cover macOS/linux (x86_64+arm64)/windows with many OS variants, Go cross-compilation and a stated Node 22.13+ floor, all built and tested.

EVO-4.note: SECURITY.md declares supported lines, which get security fixes and an explicit EOL for the 0.x middleware alphas; LTS guarantees and dated EOLs are not published, so not horizon.

OPS-1.note: caveman doctor reports one problem per line with its fix and release-smoke self-checks the build; a machine-readable repair plan is not offered, so not horizon.

OPS-2.note: Structured logging and OpenTelemetry are present (browse/proxy), and Cloud ingests OTEL/logs for observability; not uniformly wired with GenAI semantic conventions, so not horizon.

OPS-3.note: 255 environment variables are read and only ~108 appear in docs, and there is no single validated config schema, so a large configuration surface is undocumented; defaults (local-first, telemetry disclosed opt-out) are mostly safe.

OPS-4.note: Install is curl|bash / irm|iex / npx but one-liners are version-pinned (v4.0.1) and the probe finds 30 checksum/signature-verification references; binaries are cosign-signed. Not verified-by-default across every path, so not horizon.

PRV-1.note: RED LINE: not triggered. Telemetry is opt-out and content-free (counts/labels/install-id/OS/IP, never prompts/code/paths), defaults off in CI/non-TTY, honours DO_NOT_TRACK and CAVEMAN_TELEMETRY=0, prints a first-run disclosure and documents every field; IPs cleared after 90 days.

PRV-2.note: Local-first by default: the skill/engine/proxy send nothing, originals stay in local CCR, Auto/Cloud are opt-in and fully disclosed, and telemetry deletion is documented; no fully-offline residency guarantee for the managed path.

PRV-3.note: RED LINE: not triggered. Apache-2.0 LICENSE plus LICENSE-MIT, a complete NOTICE, LICENSING.md and TRADEMARKS.md; third-party notices present. Not REUSE per-file, so not horizon.

PRV-4.note: SECURITY.md and extension/PRIVACY.md address privacy and data flows thoroughly, but there is no stated position on the EU CRA or AI Act for this distributed product.

SUS-1.note: Single maintainer by the project's own statement ('One person maintains this for free'), with only a Code of Conduct and no CODEOWNERS or governance/succession process for a widely-installed CLI.

SUS-2.note: Issue templates, CI gates and conformance lanes, required DCO sign-off and a documented review process ('a maintainer checks license scope, tests, generated artifacts, and security boundaries').

SUS-3.note: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md and per-directory agent files give detailed instructions for agents working in the repo, and DCO sign-off plus maintainer review cover contributions; agent-change attribution is not separately evaluated over time.

gaps.title: Single-maintainer project with no governance
gaps.case: README.md:318 states 'One person maintains this for free'; there is no CODEOWNERS or governance doc (meta.codeowners/meta.governance), only CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, across a six-product polyglot monorepo installed widely.
gaps.impact: sustainability / supply chain: bus-factor and continuity risk for a CLI with a very large install base.
gaps.fix: Add CODEOWNERS, recruit a second maintainer and publish a governance/succession process.

gaps.title: Static analysis is uneven across the largest languages
gaps.case: CI runs only tsc --noEmit (TS types) and go vet (packages/cli/package.json:32, engine-ci.yml:29); there is no golangci-lint/staticcheck, no gofmt gate, no ESLint and no Python linter or type checker, over 93k lines of Go, 41k TS and 22k Py.
gaps.impact: maintainability: the cheapest defect filter is applied inconsistently to the bulk of the code.
gaps.fix: Add golangci-lint + gofmt gate, ruff + mypy for Python and ESLint for TS to CI.

gaps.title: Large undocumented configuration surface
gaps.case: The probe reads 255 environment variables of which only ~108 appear in docs (obs.env_vars), and there is no single validated config schema.
gaps.impact: operability: operators of the proxy/runtime face hidden settings and no schema to validate against.
gaps.fix: Document and validate every environment variable at startup and publish a config schema.

gaps.title: Flagship session number not reproducible at this commit
gaps.case: The headline '33.2% fewer input tokens' session result is, per docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md, an August-2026 older-engine run with no committed raw pairs (benchmarks/results/.gitkeep), and the evals snapshot is n=10 single-run.
gaps.impact: epistemic/reproducibility: the flagship number cannot be reproduced on the shipped engine (the doc discloses this, which lowers severity).
gaps.fix: Commit raw session pairs and re-run the session benchmark on the current engine, dated.

gaps.title: Cryptography has no inventory, abstraction or PQC plan
gaps.case: The gateway uses TLS, OIDC JWT (RS256/ES256), AWS SigV4 and AES directly (proxy/internal/identity, shared/platform/awssig) with no algorithm inventory, replaceable layer or post-quantum plan.
gaps.impact: horizon/compliance: CNSA 2.0 and the NIST 2030-35 transition are unprepared for the gateway's signing/TLS.
gaps.fix: Document a crypto inventory, route crypto through one abstraction and publish a dated ML-KEM/ML-DSA plan.

gaps.title: Mirrored source trees can drift
gaps.case: skills/ is mirrored into plugins/caveman/skills, browse/ is a declared consumer copy of another repo, and the Apache text is repeated across many directories (~86 duplicate files per the cross-repo dissection).
gaps.impact: maintainability: two copies of a skill or doc can diverge and an agent may read the stale one.
gaps.fix: Generate the mirrors at build time and assert byte-equality in CI, or single-source them.

gaps.title: SBOMs shipped but no VEX
gaps.case: Releases attach CycloneDX SBOMs (release-packages.yml:318) but emit no VEX statements for known CVEs (SEC-4).
gaps.impact: compliance: buyers cannot see which SBOM-listed CVEs are exploitable vs not-affected.
gaps.fix: Emit OpenVEX alongside each release SBOM.

opportunities.title: Extract the CCR recovery store as a standalone package
opportunities.description: The Context Recovery store (content-addressed sha256 handles, SQLite WAL, atomic/fail-closed, idempotent, byte-exact recovery) is a self-contained hub (dissection score 18). Extracted, it is a reusable recovery substrate for REA Evidence, Absurd steps and strix tool-output spill.

opportunities.title: Share one content-addressed retrieval handle with REA and strix
opportunities.description: caveman's CCR handle, REA's evidence_id and strix's tool-output spill are all content-addressed. A single retrieval-handle standard lets a compressed view, an evidence record and an agent tool result interoperate so summaries never lose the original.

opportunities.title: Consolidate token accounting into one measured budget library
opportunities.description: Offline token accounting (tiktoken o200k, honest-numbers method) is implemented here and conceptually duplicated in leanrea's context-budget, strix's context_budget and pi's compaction. One measured budget library would serve all of them.

opportunities.title: Publish the S0-S4 safety-class ladder as a transform-honesty standard
opportunities.description: The engine's S0-S4 registry (byte-safe vs model-visible, requires-CCR, reversible) plus the byte-safe passthrough contract is a reusable honesty standard any transform tool could declare against, composable with ponytail's necessity ladder as policy-as-code.

opportunities.title: Add VEX to become a CRA-complete reference for the set
opportunities.description: caveman already ships provenance, SBOMs, cosign signatures and OpenSSF Scorecard; adding OpenVEX closes the last gap and makes it a dated-obligation-ready supply-chain reference the other reviewed repos can copy.

reengineering.gain: a uniform defect filter over the whole codebase
reengineering.measure: golangci-lint + gofmt gate + ruff + mypy + ESLint run green in CI on every change
CODEOWNERS committed, at least two active maintainers and a governance/succession doc published

reengineering.gain: a reusable content-addressed recovery substrate for the reviewed set
reengineering.measure: a published package consumed by at least one other repo with a recovery round-trip parity test

reengineering.gain: no hidden configuration for proxy/runtime operators
reengineering.measure: every environment variable documented and validated at startup and a config schema published

questions: Are any of the 39 secret-like strings real secrets outside tests (SEC-6 red line)? No: all are test fixtures (well-known AWS example keys) or secret-prefix allowlists in detection/redaction code (redact.go, residual.go, repointel/index.go), confirmed by reading each non-test match; SEC-6 is 3, not a red line.

Is telemetry a red line (on by default without disclosure or collecting user content, PRV-1)? No: it is opt-out, content-free, CI/non-TTY-off, DO_NOT_TRACK-respecting, first-run-disclosed and field-documented; PRV-1 is 3.

Are the headline token-reduction claims contradicted by measurement (EPI-5 red line)? No: HONEST-NUMBERS reports net-negative cases and labels unverified numbers, and claims link to method; EPI-5 is 3, not 0.
not_examined: Runtime behaviour (static review only; nothing was executed)
The private caveman-agent-sdk, caveman-coding-agent and Caveman Cloud repositories referenced by routing
The external Adobe/JetBrains/Elastic sources cited for outside benchmarks
Full pnpm-lock/go.sum dependency audit and git history beyond HEAD (shallow clone)
